lyon-rh-ne-alpes-rides-dr-me-proven-ale-.story: Scenery first, traffic last, with checkpoints that make sense on a bike. 257 km round from Givors - plan on about 5 h 21 of riding. It goes by way of Craponne, Scenic stretch near Le Bois-d'Oingt and in Saint-Georges-de-Reneins. The climb of the day is near Saint-Didier-sous-Riverie. Much of it runs through woodland.

lyon-rh-ne-alpes-rides-dr-me-proven-ale-.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: Treat High point near Saint-Didier-sous-Riverie → Near Craponne as bend craft. Brake early, look high through the turn, and keep throttle changes gentle. It is more satisfying to link ten clean bends than rescue one silly one.

Scenic stretch near Le Bois-d'Oingt → Photo stop in Saint-Georges-de-Reneins is the reward section in Lyon. Look through the bends, use legal pull-offs for photos and keep a little margin for tractors, cyclists and damp shade. The best ride here is smooth, not noisy.

sections.to: Near Bouvesse-Quirieu, on the way back
sections.advice: Photo stop in Saint-Georges-de-Reneins → Near Bouvesse-Quirieu, on the way back is shade riding: beautiful, cooler and sometimes slick. Expect damp patches, leaves, gravel and wildlife where the trees meet the road.

sections.from: Near Bouvesse-Quirieu, on the way back

sections.advice: Food stop in Trept → Back to Drôme Provençale is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.

sections.advice: Sonora California → Dardanelle is 78 km of getting across. Ride it tidily and keep the enthusiasm for what comes after.
Dardanelle → Sonora Pass climbs about 2933 m in 21 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Sonora Pass → Bridgeport drops about 2933 m over 45 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Sonora Pass Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2933 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Sonora Pass → Bridgeport
scenicChapters.narrative: 2933 m come off over 57 km at around 6.5%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it. Brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

sonora-pass-road.story: A 182 km one-way ride from near Sonora, about 3 h of riding. On the way it passes Dardanelle and Sonora Pass. The highest point is about 2,950 m. Sonora Pass is open in summer only - check it is open before you set off. It suits an unhurried touring pace.

scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 27 km this is Grand Tour of Switzerland, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.

scenicChapters.title: Herd Hill North → The English Lake District
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 70 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

places-hadrian-s-wall-and-vallum-and-the.story: From Greenhead it runs 263 km to Greenhead; allow about 4 h 32 of riding. It goes by way of Herd Hill North, The English Lake District and back through Herd Hill North. Lakes are the scenery here.
